key_insight: Sequential evaporation follows two different solid-state conversion pathways in perovskite tandem absorbers: mixed-halide WBG films convert through a chemically mixed reservoir, while Sn-Pb NBG films form a Pb-rich phase early and retain vertical composition gradients.
engineering_relevance: This bandgap-specific conversion control enables solvent-free tuning of evaporated perovskite layers for all-perovskite tandems, supporting higher-efficiency and more manufacturable tandem solar cells.
method: Time-sliced ex situ analysis of sequentially evaporated precursor stacks
Comparative study of mixed-halide wide-bandgap and Sn-Pb narrow-bandgap conversion
Guided absorber design based on observed solid-state conversion pathways
evidence_signal: The paper reports bandgaps spanning 1.26–1.96 eV, a first evaporated all-perovskite tandem solar cell with 19.2% efficiency, and 80% average retention after 1,200 h at 65 °C.
watch_item: Vertical compositional gradients and strong dependence on absolute layer thickness suggest process sensitivity, so tight evaporation control is needed for reproducibility.
paper_title: Divergent Solid-state Conversion Pathways in Evaporated All-perovskite Tandem Solar Cells
